newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB expert expects most flooded acres to be seeded.
newsitem.headline: CWB expert expects most flooded acres to be seeded.

text.p: A Canadian Wheat Board crop expert said on Wednesday that up to 500,000 acres of mainly wheat fields in Manitoba could be flooded by the swollen Red River but most of that acreage would end up seeded this year.

"Half a million acres might get flooded but I'll state unequivocally that we will not lose half a million acres. At least 80 percent will get seeded, even if it's late," Paul Bullock, CWB weather and crop surveillance director, told Reuters.

Manitoba ordered 17,000 residents of the Red River Valley to evacuate their homes on Wednesday with some officials saying this year's flood could cover twice the area hit in 1950 and 1979, when 400 square miles were flooded.
Manitoba is one of the three main Prairie crop growing provinces of western Canada, and is a top exporter of wheat, barley, canola and other crops.
